Scottsdale Bus Rental: Executive Minibus Group Shuttle

Scottsdale Sprinters runs an executive minibus group shuttle as a chauffeured bus booked by the hour, not by the seat, for a Scottsdale or Phoenix group of 20 to 30. Two vehicles run it: the 24-seat Mini Bus (24 Pax) at $185 an hour and the 29-seat Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) at $225 an hour, both on a 4-hour minimum, so a shuttle starts at $740 before 8% tax. Below: the wave and loop patterns, what the office asks before it quotes, and where a bigger group goes. Call (623) 986-6339.

What is a Scottsdale executive minibus group shuttle?

A chauffeured bus booked by the hour for a group of 20 to 30, on two named vehicles: Mini Bus (24 Pax) at $185 an hour, Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) at $225 an hour, both on a 4-hour minimum. A shuttle starts at $740. "Shuttle" is the operative word. You buy a bus and a chauffeur for a block of hours, and inside it the vehicle runs whatever your written schedule says: one movement, out and back, or a repeating circuit. The clock is the product, not the headcount. A coach is the answer when the group arrives in one load; a shuttle is the answer when time is the constraint. One honest edge: the larger vehicle seats 29, so a 30th rider makes it a written quote. Both are executive units.

Which wave and loop shuttle patterns do we actually operate?

Two shapes, both hourly. A wave splits arrivals and departures into timed runs; a loop repeats one circuit for the hours you book. Neither is a timetable: one Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) moves 29 riders a circuit, two of them 58, and the interval is agreed in writing. The multi-vehicle shapes this company publishes describe the service exactly: "Arrival and departure runs split into waves across the vehicles" and "Several vehicles on one booking, coordinated to one schedule with one point of contact" A wave suits arrival and departure days, when the group lands across a window. Each run is a named departure with its own rider list, and the hourly block has already bought the time, so extra runs cost nothing. A loop suits the middle of a programme: hotel to venue and back — Up to 58 across 2 Executive Mini Coaches when one bus is not enough. It cannot be a printed interval, because a circuit depends on the venue: "A written movement plan before the date — vehicle by vehicle, pickup by pickup"

What does the office ask before it can quote a group shuttle?

6 questions, published rather than improvised. They cover where the group starts, how many are riding and whether that number is firm, the arrival time you actually need, accessibility, how the return is organised, and who we call on the day. Send the answers and the quote comes back in writing with the vehicles named. This is the list the desk already publishes: On what travels as well as who: "Passenger capacity is a seating limit, not cargo space. List banner cases, pop-up displays, sample boxes and crew gear when you request the quote so the fit is confirmed in writing rather than discovered at the curb." Some things are not settled at quote time: "Where a vehicle of your size may stop, and how close that is to the door — the venue sets that on the night." "Exact late-hour return waves, which settle once the headcount and the end time are real." Where the group starts: the office, one hotel, several hotels, or people making their own way to a single meeting point. How many are riding, and whether that number is confirmed or still moving. The venue address, and the arrival time you want people inside rather than the time you want to leave. Mobility and accessibility needs — a walker or wheelchair, a folding mobility scooter, a low step, a seat near the door, or a short walk from the drop point. How the night ends: everyone together at one time, or return waves as people leave. One on-site contact we can reach, so the chauffeur works from a written schedule instead of a group chat.

Which vehicle fits 20, 29 or 30-plus riders?

Up to 24 riders take the Mini Bus (24 Pax); up to 29 take the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax). From 30 the answer leaves this page: the 56-seat 56-Passenger Motorcoach in one load, or several minibuses on one reservation, quoted in writing. A group of 20 fits the Mini Bus (24 Pax) at $740; the same group in the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) costs $900 and buys 5 spare seats plus a published bag cap. Above 29 the desk takes over: "Hourly charters start at four hours on every vehicle except the 56-passenger motorcoach, which starts at five. The 56-passenger motorcoach is the largest single vehicle we run; a bigger movement is a coordinated multi-vehicle fleet on one reservation, not one larger bus. Anything the online quote cannot price — an unusual route, a multi-vehicle movement, a vehicle we hold for request only — goes to the reservations desk and comes back as a written quote before any card is charged." Both are units the owner runs in multiples: Up to 48 across 2 Mini Buses; Up to 58 across 2 Executive Mini Coaches — seat counts, not a claim about a date. If the group travels in one load, the charter bus rental guide prices the 56-Passenger Motorcoach at $325 an hour.

Which corporate, convention and airport groups use this shuttle?

Three patterns cover most of the work: conference and convention movements between a hotel and a venue, corporate day programmes across the Valley, and whole-group airport arrivals and departures. Each has a page here, and each opens on the same two vehicles at $185 and $225 an hour. Convention work is the commonest reason a group books this page rather than a coach: attendees spread across sessions, two fixed addresses, a bus earning its hours going round. The Mini Bus (24 Pax) is the value shape; the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) takes the room in one run. Corporate day programmes are the other steady pattern, priced on the corporate transportation page. Airport groups split in two: one arrival for the whole group is usually a transfer, flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off — $450 or $550, plus $50 a stop, and priced from the drive beyond that with the empty return included — while arrivals across a day are a wave. On any airport leg: "Flight tracking on airport legs" Published service areas are Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley. The charge is time rather than distance, so every city costs the same per hour.

What is included, and how do the deposit and cancellation work for 20 or more?

The vehicle, the chauffeur and the fuel, plus 8% Arizona tax and nothing else. A 50% deposit holds the bus and the balance is charged 48 hours before pickup. Every booking here is a large group, so it carries the 30-day cancellation window. The published inclusion list applies to any chauffeured booking. "A professional chauffeur on every vehicle, background- and MVR-checked" "Tax only — no booking fee, no service charge, no fuel surcharge, and gratuity never added for you" On a long day: "Free hours as the day gets longer: 7–11 hours earns 1, 12–14 earns 2, 15 or more earns 3" And: "Bottled water on board, the one complimentary amenity on every ride" Not included: checkout add-ons, hours past the window, and what a property charges for access. Two house rules matter here: "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop." and "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really." The tier is not a judgement call: 20 or more passengers, or 2 or more vehicles, is a large group in the refund code. "Groups of 20+ passengers, or any booking with two or more vehicles, carry the large-group cancellation window rather than the standard one." It refunds in full 30 or more days out, keeps the deposit to 14 days, nothing inside. These are the current published hourly rates; request a current quote for your date.

Things to know

  • What executive minibus options are published for Scottsdale groups? — This service offers only the published Mini Bus (24 Pax) for up to 24 passengers and the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) for up to 29 passengers. Select the exact bus in the booking flow; final assignment remains subject to availability and written confirmation.
  • What do the 24- and 29-passenger executive buses cost? — The 24-passenger Mini Bus (24 Pax) is $185 per hour with a four-hour minimum, a $740 base minimum vehicle-time estimate. The 29-passenger Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) is $225 per hour with a four-hour minimum, a $900 base minimum. Route- and date-specific items may change final written pricing.
  • Can the executive minibus run a shuttle loop? — A timed shuttle loop can be requested. Enter every stop, operating window, event contact, and requested frequency. Loop timing and passenger throughput are not guaranteed until access, traffic, loading areas, and the complete schedule are reviewed and confirmed in writing.
  • Does 24 or 29 passengers include luggage and equipment? — No. The published number is a passenger seating maximum. Luggage, production equipment, mobility devices, coolers, or other gear may reduce practical passenger fit and must be listed before the vehicle is confirmed.
  • Can I use both buses for a larger group? — Yes. In the online vehicle step, choose Coordinate multiple vehicles, enter the total group, and optionally list passenger groups and preferred published buses. The request remains coordinator-priced with vehicle assignment pending; no combination, fit, availability, or payment is assumed before written review.
